what_happened: Both target countermodels (Z1 and UZ over translationFrame D at arbitrary non-Archimedean D with a least positive duration) were machine-checked sorry-free during research via lean_run_code probes, together with all four least-positive entry points, the IsDiscrete glue, and the ValidOnFrames/FrameOver-D corollaries. Implementation risk is near zero; the plan can transcribe verified proof text.

Post-788 doc drift: Axiom.z1 no longer exists in the base Axiom inductive (only prior_UZ carries .ZTime; Z1 is the derived CompletenessDerived.z1Thm), yet five docstrings still name Axiom.z1 - ProofSystem/Axioms.lean:541 ('ZTime (2 axioms: prior_UZ, z1)'), Semantics/FrameProperty.lean (IsZTime docstring), Metalogic/Conservativity.lean:113, Metalogic/Independence.lean:80, Metalogic/Independence/StaticFrame.lean:55/300/303. Not blocking this task; new docstrings must use post-788 names.

The '% PORT:' marker named by the dispatch lives in /home/benjamin/Philosophy/Papers/PossibleWorlds/JPL/possible_worlds.tex, outside this repository's working tree; the dispatch also assigns the prop:archimedean rewording to PossibleWorlds task 172. Raised as a non-blocking user_decision rather than silently edited or silently dropped.

Task 790's isDiscrete_iff_exists_isLeast_pos and succOrderOfIsLeastPos, landed after the research report was written, made two of the report's four planned hypothesis-entry wrappers redundant; the plan drops them and routes the Discrete-hypothesis entry through the existing lemma instead of duplicating a theorem committed three commits earlier.

Three files this task must touch are inside concurrent task 792's declared file_scope: typst/generated/status.typ (forced by typst-sync-check check 2 once a new .lean file lands), docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md (the prop:archimedean KNOWN-ANCHORS row says the repo does not check the anchor, which this task falsifies), and FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/README.md. Plan carries a re-read-then-inspect protocol plus reasoned-exclusion fallbacks for the two ungated ones.

The plan deferred typst/generated/status.typ regeneration to Phase 4, but .githooks/pre-commit is a BLOCKING build-free gate that refuses any commit staging a .lean path while typst-sync-check Check 2 has drifted. Phase 1's two additions moved formalsystem-line-count by 58, so the regeneration had to move forward to every .lean commit. scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix produced exactly the two expected lines plus the stamp, no foreign edits.

The research report's Appendix carried both countermodel proof bodies as text already compiled sorry-free by lean_run_code, and the one body it did not carry verbatim (the order lemma) recompiled first try with zero diagnostics. Phase 1 was transcription with no proof search at all.

Phase 2's 381-line module compiled on the first guarded build attempt with zero errors, including the one piece of glue the plan flagged as uncertain (whether isDiscrete_iff_exists_isLeast_pos's .mp unifies through TaskFrame.IsDiscrete -- it does, so the documented fallback was unused). Attributable to the research report having compiled both countermodel bodies with lean_run_code before the plan was written.

Phase 3's Scope Hypothesis named 7 Axiom.z1 occurrences across 5 files, derived by grep at plan time. The pre-edit re-grep found 9 across 7: Semantics/FrameClassValidity.lean and MinusLanguage/Axioms.lean also referenced the removed constructor. Both were admitted under the phase's own 'treat any new occurrence as in scope' rule. Separately, StarLanguage/Axioms.lean matches the same grep pattern but names StarAxiom.z1/PlusAxiom.z1, constructors that genuinely exist -- a substring false positive the plan's pattern did not distinguish.

The full guarded build took roughly 40 minutes of wall time, dominated by one module: FormalSystem.Metalogic.Decidability.Verified.Termination.SubformulaProperty elaborated for 1103s on its own, with MintBound.OrderingTimes at 161s and Verified.Decidable at 56s behind it. Nothing in this task touches the Decidability tree; the cost is a fixed toll any task needing a whole-tree build pays, and it required five successive bounded waiter calls to sit out.

Self-inflicted plan corruption while closing Phase 4: the close script sliced the plan with s.index('## Lean Challenge Statements'), but that exact heading text ALSO appears as an inline backticked mention inside the Goals bullet ('the identifier set pinned under `## Lean Challenge Statements` below'). The index matched the earlier prose occurrence, so the slice boundary landed before Phase 1 and the rewrite duplicated phases 1-3, inflating the plan from 692 to 1060 lines. Detected immediately by the post-edit heading grep. Recovered by rewriting the file from 'git show HEAD:<plan>' and re-applying every marker, checkbox and deviation annotation with LINE-based section boundaries derived from ^### Phase and ^## matches instead of substring indices. Lesson: never slice a markdown artifact by substring index on a heading string -- a plan routinely quotes its own section names in prose.

A one-line docstring fix applied AFTER the inventory currency check had passed cascaded into three gate findings on the first full check-module-invariants run: C28 (a 144-column line in Semantics/FrameClassValidity.lean, from a bad re-wrap of the Axiom.z1 amendment), INV (the root README's generated inventory block gone stale on the +1 comment line), and C35 (four declaration spans in scripts/lean-citation-manifest.json shifted by the ZTimeSharpness docstring edit). All three were mechanical and this task's own; fixing them forced a second full-tree rebuild, since the amended module sits deep in the Semantics import graph. Lesson: batch every prose edit BEFORE running the generators, not after.

check-module-invariants.sh earned its cost here: it caught all three of this task's residual mechanical defects (an over-long line, a stale generated inventory block, and four shifted citation-manifest spans) that no build, no sorry census and no reading of the diff would have surfaced, and each came with the exact regeneration command as the remedy.
